verdict.rationale: Terraform's documentation describes defining infrastructure in 'human-readable configuration files' written in HCL, a domain-specific configuration language rather than a general-purpose programming language. Community comments confirm HCL has loop-like constructs (for_each, dynamic blocks) but call it a 'half-baked language'. One user contrasts it with 'a real programming language', and another complains about weak navigation and discoverability. The pack has no evidence of a first-party way to write Terraform infrastructure in a general-purpose language with types and IDE support, so the applicable axis is unmet.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define infrastructure in a general-purpose programming language with types, loops, and IDE support
